head: ai-replay-budget-r2
report:
Running the three replays in parallel while reading the diff.

I found two defects at this head. The previous round's four findings are all closed: I copied its probes unchanged and ran them against this head.

## DEFECT: A Codex websocket reconnect refused by the budget turns off websockets for the whole session

**Mechanism.** At this head, `openCodexWebSocketTransport` (`openai-codex-responses.ts:1967`) checks the budget again just before sending: `if (replayOf !== undefined && !admitsReplay(requestContext.replayBudget, 0)) throw replayOf;`. Here `replayOf` is `#replayOf`, the stream failure being recovered from. When the websocket drops mid-stream, that failure is a `CodexWebSocketTransportError` (for example `websocket closed (1006)` at :4117, or `websocket closed before response completion` at :4299).

`#reopenWebSocketStream` (:3289–3318) wraps that call in a catch for `CodexWebSocketTransportError`. The catch handles any such error as a failed reopen: it calls `recordCodexWebSocketFailure(state, true)`, which sets `state.disableWebsocket = true` and closes the socket that was just opened. Nothing in the provider ever sets `disableWebsocket` back to false, and `shouldUseCodexWebSocket` (:3618) returns false while it is set. So when the budget refuses a reconnect, every later turn in the session runs over SSE, even though no reconnect was sent.

This also overrides a decision the provider already made. `#tryReplayWebsocketFailureOverSse` (:3148–3177) computed `activateFallback = false` for a first, non-fatal drop and called `recordCodexWebSocketFailure(state, false)` so it could retry on the websocket. Then `#reopenSseStream` throws the same `replayOf`, because the refusal latches, so the turn fails anyway. The only lasting effect of the refusal is that websockets are off.

**Trigger.**
- Set `replayBudgetMs` on a Codex call over websocket. For example, the coding agent's 2 s held-retry budget.
- Have the first websocket stream close before any content arrives.
- The budget admits the reconnect wait (`CODEX_WEBSOCKET_RETRY_DELAY_MS`), but the deadline passes before the send-time check. This happens if the timer wakes late, or more realistically if `getOrCreateCodexWebSocketConnection` takes long to open the new socket, since that runs before the check.
- After the call fails with `replayBudgetExhausted: true`, `state.disableWebsocket === true`, and the next call on the same session never uses websockets.

**Evidence.** I traced this through the code above; I did not run a probe for it. Before this patch, `#reopenWebSocketStream` could only reach the catch after a real reopen failure. The refusal should be rethrown before the fallback runs, for example by checking `error === this.#replayOf` before `recordCodexWebSocketFailure`.

## DEFECT: The new held-retry test fails depending on timing

**Mechanism.** In `packages/ai/test/replay-budget-wire.test.ts:435-461`, the bounded half of the test makes real sleeps of about 0.375–0.5 s and 0.75–1 s, with random jitter. It then asserts `bounded.requests() === 3` and `elapsedMs < 2_000` against a 2 s budget. That is roughly 1.1–1.5 s of real sleep plus a localhost round trip per request.

If the second timer wakes late, or the machine is busy, one of two things happens:
- the send-time check refuses the third request, so there are 2 requests, or
- the elapsed time goes past 2000 ms.

Either way the test fails.

**Measured.**
- I ran `bun test test/replay-budget-wire.test.ts test/empty-completion-retry.test.ts test/request-compression.test.ts test/github-copilot-headers.test.ts` from `packages/ai` in the same command as the utils and coding-agent tests.
- That run reported `(fail) a held retry's 2 s budget against the Anthropic provider's ceiling > spends 11 requests and over 41 s of backoff without it, and 3 requests inside 2 s with it [2148.64ms]`; the other 155 tests passed.
- Run alone it passed (1458 ms), and three more runs of the four files also passed.
- I didn't capture which assertion failed. The 2148 ms duration fits the elapsed-time check, or a late refusal after the deadline.

The wait sizes should come from the injected `providerRetryWait`, with real time kept only for the send-time check, or the timing margins should not hinge on jitter.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Previous round's findings.** I copied `probes.test.ts`, `extra.test.ts`, `resume.test.ts`, `lanes.ts` and `resume-fixture.ts` unchanged into scratch, linked them to this head's `node_modules`, and ran them with bun 1.4.4 under `env -i`.
- **Finding 1 (requests after the deadline): closed.**
  - `late-wakeup` sends 1 request with the marker set on all seven HTTP lanes.
  - `extended-provider-wait` (Anthropic) sends 1 request with the marker.
  - `late-prepare` makes 1 call with the marker.
  - `cursor-late-wait` sends 1 request with the marker.
- **Finding 2 (server waits bypassed): closed.**
  - `short-header-long-body` and `long-header-short-body` send 1 request with the marker on all four lanes.
  - For Gemini, `alternate-endpoint-hint` makes 1 call with the marker.
  - `over-provider-cap` is unmarked on Anthropic and openai-responses. That is correct, because the provider would have refused the over-cap wait anyway.
- **Finding 3 (unconditional first resume poll): closed.**
  - `resume.test.ts` sees only the initial POST and finishes in 150 ms instead of 12 s.
  - The previous round's characterization test, `resume always issues its first check even with a refused budget`, now fails (0 fetches). Its manifest said a fix would make it fail.
- **Finding 4 (false-positive marker): closed.** `own-correction-ceiling` is unmarked in both the 10000 ms and the 100 ms arm.
- Overall: 92/93 probes pass, and the single failure is that expected test; 3/3 extra and 1/1 resume pass.

**Suspicions I ruled out.**
- **`fetchWithRetry` holding the failed response.** `pending` is released before every send and when a wait is aborted. A response whose retry is refused comes back with an unread body, and the bare `signal.aborted` throw in the network branch runs only after `pending` was already cleared.
- **Where the budget is checked inside conditions.** Every `admitsReplay` call in a condition (Bedrock prefix binding, Anthropic strict tools, fallback credit, cache_control, openai-responses transient retry, Cursor) is the last operand. So a refusal is only recorded when the provider would actually have replayed.
- **The nested budget in `withReplaySafeStreamRetry`.** It hands each attempt `remainingMs()` and skips its own replay when the inner attempt already used up the budget.
- **Forwarding `replayBudgetMs`.** It reaches the providers through `mapOptionsForApi`, `pi-native-server` `ALLOWED_OPTION_KEYS`, factory-droid, gitlab-duo, and the spread in `settings-stream-fn`. All three Cursor continuation sites pass `replayBudget` and `replayOf`.
- **Turn recovery.** `consumeHeldRetryReplayBudget` only applies to the matching `provider/id` and is cleared on reset and on failure. `sameModelWaitMs` is computed after `delayMs` has been adjusted. With the default `baseDelayMs` of 500, the first retry's wait stays under the 2 s threshold, so the hold still happens.
- **Gemini endpoint switch waiting for the server's hint under a budget.** The comment marks it as deliberate, and the previous round asked for it.
- **Focused tests.** `fetch-retry.test.ts` passed 43/43. `agent-session-held-retry-replay-budget.test.ts` and `agent-session-retry-recovery.test.ts` passed 15/15. The ai test files passed 155/156, with the one failure described above.
- **First replay attempts.** These failed because the `mise` bun shim doesn't work with an empty `HOME`. That was an environment problem, not part of the change, and I reran with the real bun binary.
